title: Merge Into the Padded List
statement:
You get two lists sorted in non-decreasing order. The first, a, has length m + n: its first m entries are real values and its last n entries are 0 placeholders. The second, b, has exactly n values.

Merge b into a in place so that a holds all m + n values in sorted order. Return nothing; the checker reads a afterwards.

examples.why: The two trailing zeros are only room for b's values; they are not part of the data.
With m = 0 the single 0 is a placeholder, so it must not appear in the answer.
Every value in b is smaller, so all of a's values have to shift right. Filling from the back handles this without overwriting anything.

hints: Merging from the front means you might overwrite values in a that you still need. Where is there free space?
The free space is at the back of a. Which value belongs in the very last slot?
Walk three pointers from the back: the last real value of a, the last value of b, and the write position. Put the larger one at the write position. Stop when b is used up.

explain.intuition:
The usual merge writes the smallest value first, at the front. Here the front of a is full of values you have not read yet, so writing there would destroy them. The empty space is at the back.

So merge backwards: the largest remaining value goes into the last free slot. The write position is always at or past the read position in a, because there are exactly as many free slots behind it as values of b still to place. Nothing unread is ever overwritten. Once b is empty, the rest of a is already in place.
steps: While j ≥ 0: if i ≥ 0 and a[i] > b[j], write a[i] at w and move i; otherwise write b[j] and move j.
When j drops below 0, stop: the remaining values of a are already in place.
pitfalls: Merging from the front and overwriting values of a before reading them.
Looping while i ≥ 0 instead of while j ≥ 0. If a runs out first, the leftover values of b still need copying.
Treating the placeholder zeros as real values, especially when m = 0.

solutions.title: Copy in, then sort
solutions.idea: Overwrite the placeholders with b and sort the whole array. Correct, but ignores that both halves are already sorted.
solutions.space: O(1) to O(m + n), depending on the sort

solutions.title: Three pointers from the back
solutions.idea: The free space is at the end, so place the largest remaining value there first.

followups: Why is this backwards merge stable, or can you make it stable, if equal values carry different labels?
